about.title: Temecula Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Temecula's traffic has a rhythm of its own. Wine-country visitors, Old Town weekends, and the daily push up I-15 and back all share the same handful of roads. In 2025, the city's final tally showed 451 injury collisions, 631 people hurt, and 8 lives lost. Public records point to Winchester Road, I-15 Northbound, Rancho California Road, and Margarita Road as the corridors where the largest share of those crashes were logged, and Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to see the heaviest concentration. If one of those numbers now includes you, the next few weeks matter. Medical visits, photos of the scene, and the police report can all become evidence. Before any of that, though, the other driver's insurer will likely call. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent personal injury attorney in Riverside County who handles car accident claims on contingency, so you can focus on healing while someone else handles the paperwork.

whyChoose.title: Why Temecula Drivers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: The clock is shorter than most people think
items.desc: California generally allows two years to file a car accident injury claim, but if a city, county, or Caltrans vehicle or roadway is involved, a government claim can be due in as little as six months. An early connection helps make sure nothing is missed.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you shared some blame for a crash on Rancho California Road or anywhere else. Your recovery is reduced by your share, not erased.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in our network handles car accident cases on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life in ordinary auto claims. Our connection service costs you nothing.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other side's insurer a recorded statement, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to minimize your claim. Keep any conversation brief, stick to basic contact and policy details, and let a lawyer handle the rest.

items.question: I was hit on I-15 near Temecula by a driver from out of the area. Does that change my claim?
items.answer: Not in a way that should discourage you. Many crashes on the I-15 corridor through Temecula involve commuters and visitors from San Diego, Orange County, or beyond, and their insurance still answers for the harm they cause here. An attorney can track down the correct policy, deal with an out-of-town carrier, and make sure the CHP report is obtained and preserved.

items.question: What evidence should I hold on to after a Temecula crash?
items.answer: Save everything: photos of the vehicles and the intersection, dashcam footage, the exchange of information, medical discharge papers, and receipts for any out-of-pocket costs. Write down what you remember while it is fresh, including the time of day and weather. Do not repair your car or delete phone footage until an attorney has had a chance to review it.
